draft.title: Generating alternating current
card: When a magnet moves relative to a coil of wire, a voltage is made in the wire. This is called electromagnetic induction. If the wire is part of a complete circuit, a current flows.
Turning a magnet inside a coil, or turning a coil near a magnet, makes the current change direction again and again. This is alternating current (AC).
A generator is built this way. A shaft spins the magnet or the coil, so the magnet's movement is transformed into electrical energy.
In a power station, the shaft is turned by a turbine, a wheel with blades that spins when a moving fluid pushes on it. The turbine is joined to the generator.
draft.remember: Spin a magnet and a coil past each other to induce an alternating current. Power stations use a turbine to do the spinning.

a.q: A student spins a magnet inside a coil that is joined to a small lamp in a complete circuit. What makes the current in the coil?
opts: The magnet moving relative to the coil
The magnet sitting still inside the coil
The coil being heated by the magnet
The magnet's weight pressing on the coil
a.why: A voltage is induced when the magnet moves relative to the coil, and a complete circuit lets a current flow. A magnet that is still induces nothing, however close it is to the coil.
a.clue: Think about what must change between the magnet and the coil.

b.q: At a power station in the Latrobe Valley, a turbine is joined by a shaft to a generator. What is the job of the turbine in making alternating current?
opts: It spins the magnet or coil in the generator
It stores the current until it is needed
It makes the current flow in one direction
It makes the magnet in the generator
b.why: The turbine is pushed round by a moving fluid and turns the shaft, which spins the magnet or coil. The current is induced in the generator, not made by the turbine itself. The current changes direction because of the spinning, so it is not one direction.
b.clue: The turbine turns something. What does it turn?

wants.brief: A simple generator: a bar magnet on a shaft spinning inside a coil of wire, with the coil joined to a lamp in a complete circuit. Label: magnet, coil, shaft, lamp.
wants.why: It shows that the moving magnet and the coil are the parts that make the current.

a.best: The magnet moving relative to the coil

b.best: It spins the magnet or coil in the generator

problems.detail: The third line says the shaft spins 'the magnet or the coil', then says 'the magnet's movement is transformed into electrical energy'. When the coil is the part that spins, this is wrong. Better: 'the kinetic energy of the spinning part is transformed into electrical energy'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, each with one clear right answer, and the explanations agree with the card. One small wording slip: the card says only the magnet's movement becomes electrical energy, though it has just said the coil may be the part that spins.
